Violin plot of genes or per-cell values

Source: R/distribution_plots.R
VlnPlot_bioToolkit.Rd

Draws the distribution of one or more features in each group of cells as violins, with a box of the inter-quartile range and median and a sample of the cells as points. Features can be genes, metadata columns (QC metrics, module scores) or a mix, each in its own panel with its own axis. A drop-in alternative to Seurat::VlnPlot() with a fixed size: save it with save_plot; the values behind it are returned by export_source_data.

Usage

VlnPlot_bioToolkit(
  object,
  features,
  group.by = NULL,
  split.by = NULL,
  split.by.cols = NULL,
  split.by.side = c("opposite", "labels"),
  group.bar.width = 3.5,
  cells = NULL,
  assay = NULL,
  slot = "data",
  flip = FALSE,
  stack = FALSE,
  log = FALSE,
  percent = FALSE,
  y.max = NULL,
  zeros = c("include", "exclude", "annotate"),
  box = TRUE,
  box.width = 0.2,
  pt.n = 1500,
  pt.size = 0.16,
  alpha = 0.4,
  adjust = 1,
  cols = NULL,
  italic.genes = TRUE,
  ncol = NULL,
  cell.width = 0.35,
  cell.height = 0.35,
  panel.width = NULL,
  panel.height = NULL,
  raster = NULL,
  raster.dpi = 1000,
  seed = 42,
  legend.position = "none",
  bg = "transparent"
)

Arguments

object

A Seurat object, or a data frame with one row per cell (e.g. a table of QC metrics; row names are the cell names)

features

Features to plot: genes, metadata columns, module scores or embedding dimensions (from a data frame: its numeric columns). Gene symbols are matched exactly (rat and mouse "Cd3e", human "CD3E"); missing ones are left out with a warning

group.by

Column to group cells by: one violin per group, filled with the group's colour. If NULL (default), the active identities of a Seurat object, or one group for a data frame

split.by

Column of a higher-level grouping, drawn like facets: one labelled block of violins per level, e.g. `group.by = "condition", split.by = "cell_type"` compares conditions within each cell type. Default is NULL. (Seurat's `split.by` dodges violins instead)

split.by.cols

Colours of the bars marking the `split.by` blocks: NULL (default) for black bars, a qualitative palette name, or colours named by level of `split.by`

split.by.side

Side of the `split.by` blocks: "opposite" (default; opposite the group names: on top, or on the right with `flip = TRUE`) or "labels" (beyond the group names)

group.bar.width

Thickness of the `split.by` bars in points, default is 3.5

cells

Cells to use, as names or indices. If NULL (default), all

assay

Assay to read genes from. If NULL (default), the default assay; the assay and layer used are reported in a message when a feature is a gene, and written to the source data

slot

Layer to read genes from, default is "data"

flip

Whether to draw horizontal violins (groups on the y-axis, the first at the top), default is FALSE (vertical, groups on x)

stack

Whether to stack the features as thin panels sharing the group axis (rows; columns when flipped), default is FALSE (one panel each, in a grid of `ncol` columns)

log

Whether to draw values on a log10 axis: TRUE / FALSE for all features, or the names of the features to draw so (e.g. `c("nCount_RNA", "nFeature_RNA")`). Values of 0 or below cannot be drawn and are left out, with a message. Default is FALSE

percent

Whether values are fractions (0 to 1) shown as percentages on the axis: TRUE / FALSE, or the names of the features (e.g. "mito_fraction"). Default is FALSE

y.max

Top of the value axis: a number, a quantile of each feature's values such as "q99" (zooms past a few extreme cells), or NULL (default) for the full range. Only the view is cut: violins and boxes are computed from all cells and cut at the top of the axis, and points above it are not drawn. One value for all features, or a vector named by feature

zeros

How cells with a value of 0 are handled for genes: "include" (default, as Seurat), "exclude" (violins of the cells above 0 only) or "annotate" (as "exclude", with the % of cells above 0 printed for each group). Not applied to other features

box

Whether to draw the box (inter-quartile range and median), default is TRUE

box.width

Width of the box, as a fraction of a violin's slot, default is 0.2

pt.n

Largest number of cells drawn as points per violin, picked at random (`seed`), default is 1500. 0 draws no points; Inf all

pt.size

Size of the points, default is 0.16

alpha

Opacity of the points, default is 0.4

adjust

Bandwidth multiplier of the densities, default is 1

cols

Colours of the groups: NULL (default) for the colours DimPlot_bioToolkit gives them ("scanpy-20" up to 20 groups), a qualitative palette name, or colours named by group (or in level order)

italic.genes

Whether gene names are set in italics, default is TRUE

ncol

Number of columns of panels when `stack = FALSE`. If NULL (default), as Seurat

cell.width, cell.height

Width (vertical violins) or height (horizontal violins) of one violin's slot in inches, default is 0.35

panel.width, panel.height

Length of the value axis in inches: the panel height for vertical violins and the width for horizontal ones. If NULL (default), 1.6, or 0.5 when stacked

raster

Whether to rasterize the points: NULL (default) does so above 2000 points; or TRUE / FALSE

raster.dpi

Resolution of rasterized points, default is 1000

seed

Random seed of the sampled and jittered points, default is 42

legend.position

Position of the group legend, default is "none" (the groups are named on the axis)

bg

Background colour, default is "transparent"

Value

A ggplot object for one feature, otherwise a patchwork

Details

Cells without a value of `group.by` (or `split.by`) are left out, with a message. Group colours are taken from all levels of `group.by` in the whole object, so that they match an embedding of all cells.

The source data (export_source_data) hold one row per cell and feature: `cell`, `group`, `split`, `feature`, `value`, whether the cell is `drawn` (`zeros`, `log`) and, for genes, the `assay` and `layer`.

See also

RidgePlot_bioToolkit, DotPlot_bioToolkit, save_plot, export_source_data

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# QC metrics per sample, from the metadata alone
VlnPlot_bioToolkit(obj[[]], c("nCount_RNA", "nFeature_RNA", "percent.mt"),
                   group.by = "sample", log = c("nCount_RNA", "nFeature_RNA"))

# Genes per cell type, horizontal
VlnPlot_bioToolkit(obj, c("Cdh5", "Col1a1"), group.by = "cell_type",
                   assay = "SCT", flip = TRUE)

# Conditions compared within each cell type; % above 0 for sparse genes
VlnPlot_bioToolkit(obj, "Nppa", group.by = "condition",
                   split.by = "cell_type", zeros = "annotate")

# Many markers, stacked
p <- VlnPlot_bioToolkit(obj, c("Cdh5", "Col1a1", "Myh6", "Cd74"),
                        group.by = "cell_type", stack = TRUE, pt.n = 0)
save_plot(p, "violins.pdf")
} # }
